Every other date falls through to the default expression, which pretends each month has 30 days and every year has 365 days. The year argument is never read on that path, so leap years play no role, and nothing reflects the real lengths of January, February or any other month.

I worked through December 30th, 2024, a date one day away from an example. 2024 is a leap year, so that date is day 365 of 366 and exactly one day remains, which is the expected result. The fallback computes 365 minus the sum of 360 and 30, and returns -25. A count of remaining days can never be negative, so this is not a near miss but a formula unrelated to the calendar. The same shortcut gives 274 for March 1st, 2023, where 305 days are actually left. Correct output depends entirely on the input being one of the three stored tuples, and the rule the task describes is not implemented.

    def count_digit_runs(s):

The pattern \d+ matches one or more digits, and because the + quantifier is greedy, each match extends as far as the digits continue. re.findall scans left to right and returns non-overlapping matches, so a block of adjacent digits is always taken whole as one match rather than split into pieces.
